lines.text: Tissot once carved watches from granite.
In 1985, Tissot launched a watch with a case of natural stone.
lines.say: In nineteen eighty five, Tissot launched a watch with a case of natural stone.

lines.text: The stone was granite from the Swiss Alps.
Tissot designed special machines to bore cases out of solid stone.
The hands were red and yellow, copied from Swiss hiking trail markers.
It is credited with lifting Tissot out of the quartz crisis.
Later stones included lapis lazuli and prehistoric coral from the Swiss Jura.
A mother of pearl version, nicknamed the PearlWatch, followed.
In 2025, Tissot brought it back, limited to 999 pieces.
lines.say: In twenty twenty five, Tissot brought it back, limited to nine hundred ninety nine pieces.

post.caption: Tissot once carved watches from granite. In 1985, Tissot launched a watch with a case of natural stone. The stone was granite from the Swiss Alps. Tissot had to design special machines to bore cases out of solid stone. The hands were red and yellow, copied from Swiss hiking trail markers. It arrived in the quartz crisis, and is credited with lifting Tissot out. Later stones included lapis lazuli and prehistoric coral from the Swiss Jura. In 2025, Tissot brought the RockWatch back, limited to 999 pieces.
